extracted.intended_audience: general readers interested in satire/critique of Christian Science and Mary Baker Eddy
extracted.subtask_description: A late-19th/early-20th-century satirical essay enumerating and criticizing the by-laws, governance, publishing practices, and cultic trappings of Mary Baker Eddy's Christian Science movement. The text mixes quotation of rules with ironical commentary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compulsory hymn-singing by-law
rubrics_metrics.description: The Mother Church requires the singing of one of Mrs. Eddy's three hymns 'as often as once each month.' If a solo singer 'shall neglect or refuse to sing alone' one of those hymns as often as once a month (or oftener if directed), the singer's salary shall be stopped.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authorial commentary: the by-law is presented as evidence that Mrs. Eddy foresaw that singers would get tired of repeating long hymns and therefore imposed compulsion with penalty; repetition is noted as wearisome and the by-law a measure 'born of experience, not foresight.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Board of Education composition & control
rubrics_metrics.description: The Board of Education consists of four members, one of whom is President; members are elected annually 'subject to Mrs. Eddy's approval.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commentary: the text interprets this as Mrs. Eddy 'owning' the Board and effectively re-electing herself via control of appointments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public teachers admission exam
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants for public-teacher admission must pass a thorough three days' examination before the Board of Education covering: 'Science and Health, chapter on
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The author quotes the required passages (Recapitulation; Platform of Christian Science; specific page-and-paragraph ranges of Science and Health) to show the exact, narrow canonical texts candidates must memorise and be examined on.

rubrics_metrics.name: Board of Lectureship territory and approval
rubrics_metrics.description: Lecturers are assigned an appointed territory (North, South, East, West, Canada, Great Britain, etc.) and 'must stick to his own territory and not forage beyond its boundaries.' No lecture is delivered until Mrs. Eddy has examined and approved it, and the lecturer is not allowed to change it afterwards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commentary: the author frames lecturers as 'exceedingly important servants' chosen by Mrs. Eddy, elected annually 'subject to the approval of Rev. Mary Baker G. Eddy,' emphasizing tight central control over content and assignment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Missionaries: limited number and annual election
rubrics_metrics.description: There are only four missionaries; they are elected annually.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commentary: presented to illustrate that no servant has a truly independent, steady job except Mrs. Eddy, underscoring centralized personal control.

rubrics_metrics.name: Branch Churches forbidden to use (some) By-laws
rubrics_metrics.description: The By-laws state that 'The branch Churches are strictly forbidden to use them.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Author's note: the statement is rendered absurd because the By-laws themselves are 'the voice of the master issuing commands to the servants' and branch churches have no institutionally available mechanism to re-utter or exercise those By-laws independently.

rubrics_metrics.name: Creed is copyrighted and immutable
rubrics_metrics.description: The Creed is copyrighted by Mrs. Eddy and it is forbidden to change the Creed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commentary: author remarks on the oddity of copyrighting a Creed and forbidding any change — a legal lock on doctrine.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aggressive copyright practice
rubrics_metrics.description: Mrs. Eddy habitually copyrights early editions and revisions of her works (Science and Health and other writings) and maintains persistent copyright claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discussion: the author criticizes the ongoing drive to copyright even minor material and muses about attempting to secure perpetual copyright via legal/political influence; points out tension between ephemeral copyright and claims of perennial revelation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publishing Association: gift with 'string' clause (reclaim power)
rubrics_metrics.description: Mrs. Eddy donated the Christian Science Journal and Publishing Society to an association, but included contractual provisions ('string-clause') allowing her to reclaim the property under certain conditions (e.g., dissolution).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Author recounts historical example (Nixon's stewardship) and the later reclaiming of the Journal as evidence Mrs. Eddy structured gifts so she retained practical control.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publishing Society governance and appointment control
rubrics_metrics.description: The publishing business is put into the hands of a special publishing Board; Mrs. Eddy appoints to its vacancies. Editors and publishers cannot be elected or removed without Mrs. Eddy's knowledge and consent. Every candidate for employment in the publishing house must be 'accepted by Mrs. Eddy as suitable.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The text emphasizes transfer of financial benefits to the Mother-Church (which the author calls 'Mrs. Eddy') and the centralization of personnel decisions to her, implying lack of independent governance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Local Self-Government clause (Mother-Church)
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Local Self-Government. The First Church of Christ, Scientist, in Boston, Massachusetts, shall assume no official control of other churches of this denomination. It shall be officially controlled by no other church.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Author interprets the clause as disingenuous: despite the wording, other By-laws ensure the Mother-Church (and Mrs. Eddy) keeps autocratic control over branch churches; the statement is rhetorical mask for centralized power.

rubrics_metrics.name: Branch Church founding prerequisite: organizer must be accredited pupil
rubrics_metrics.description: A branch Church must be organized 'in the one and only permissible way--by a member, in good standing, of the Mother-Church, and who is also a pupil of one of Mrs. Eddy's accredited students.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Author highlights this requirement as a property/ownership clause that ensures churches are composed of 'her properties' and remain doctrinally controlled.

rubrics_metrics.name: Branch Church: membership must sign and pledge Creed furnished by Mrs. Eddy
rubrics_metrics.description: The new Church cannot enter upon its functions until its members have individually signed and pledged allegiance to a Creed furnished by Mrs. Eddy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The author uses this to show enforced doctrinal uniformity and lack of independent belief among branches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Branch Church: required study and prohibition on outside religious works
rubrics_metrics.description: Branch Churches are obliged to study Mrs. Eddy's books and order their lives by them and 'must read no outside religious works.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interpretation: this rule enforces doctrinal isolation, controlling members' religious reading and formation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Branch Church: authorized hymns and prayers only
rubrics_metrics.description: Branch Churches must sing the hymns and pray the prayers provided by Mrs. Eddy and use no others in the services except by her permission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Author notes this eliminates liturgical freedom and enforces uniform ritual vocabulary across branches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Branch Church: no preachers or pastors
rubrics_metrics.description: Branch Churches are forbidden from having preachers and pastors (Mrs. Eddy's law).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The essay treats this as part of replacing human pastoral offices with central authorities (and ultimately with the book as 'Pastor-Universal').

rubrics_metrics.name: Branch Church: two Readers requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: In each branch Church they must have two Readers—a man and a woman.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Presented as a specific liturgical/officer requirement imposed centrally.

rubrics_metrics.name: Branch Church: services must use Mrs. Eddy's framed services
rubrics_metrics.description: Branch Churches must read the services framed and appointed by Mrs. Eddy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Another liturgical control mechanism; the author catalogs this among the comprehensive list of functions over which the Mother-Church rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appointment & dismissal of Readers by Mother-Church
rubrics_metrics.description: Mrs. Eddy (not the branch Church) appoints the Readers and also dismisses them and fills vacancies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Author stresses that appointment and removal can be done without consulting the branch Church or offering explanation, illustrating unilateral central power.

rubrics_metrics.name: Branch Church lectures: permission & selection by Mrs. Eddy
rubrics_metrics.description: A branch Church can have a religious lecture only by applying to Mrs. Eddy; the branch Church cannot select the lecturer—Mrs. Eddy does it—and the branch Church pays the lecturer's fee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The text treats this as a means of controlling public teaching and revenue flow while maintaining nominally local events.

rubrics_metrics.name: Christian Science wedding-teams licensing
rubrics_metrics.description: All Christian Science wedding-teams (members of branch Churches) must be 'duly authorized and consecrated Christian Science functionaries' licensed by Mrs. Eddy's factory.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Author frames marriage rites as another church function monopolized by the Mother-Church's licensing apparatus.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unspecified matters infer default positions (christenings & funerals)
rubrics_metrics.description: Nothing is said in the By-laws about christenings (inferable that a child is born a Christian Scientist and needs no ritual) or funerals (inferable that a branch Church may choose in that matter).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Author notes these absences and offers inferred doctrinal/practical consequences, underscoring the thoroughness of listed controls and the few remaining open matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: List of trivial liberties retained by branch Churches
rubrics_metrics.description: The branch Churches retain only a few 'unmeddled-with liberties': (1) appoint furnace-stoker in winters; (2) appoint fan-distributors in summers; (3) choose whether to burn/bury/preserve members supposedly dead; (4) take up a collection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Author's ironic summation: the liberties are trivial and do not grant meaningful self-government.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mother-Church Unique (no branch may have branches)
rubrics_metrics.description: The By-law 'Mother-Church Unique' declares the Mother-Church stands alone, 'occupies a position that no other Church can fill,' and therefore no branch Church is allowed to have branches.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Author presents this as an attempt to monopolize ecclesiastical prestige and to prevent any rival 'St. Peter's' for Christian Science outside Boston.

rubrics_metrics.name: No First Members (exclusive organizational form for Mother-Church)
rubrics_metrics.description: Branch Churches shall not organize with 'First Members'; that special method of organization is adapted to the Mother-Church alone.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Author notes this as a legal mechanism preserving exclusive honors and creating dependence of branches on the Mother-Church's special status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Article 'The' reserved for Mother-Church
rubrics_metrics.description: The article 'The' must not be used before the titles of branch Churches nor written on applications for membership in naming such churches. The capitalized 'The' is to be used only for the Mother-Church.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Author treats this as a petty but symbolically important restriction reserving rhetorical prestige (the word 'The') for the Mother-Church alone.

rubrics_metrics.name: Life-term monopoly on human Pastor
rubrics_metrics.description: There is but one human Pastor in the whole Christian Science world; Mrs. Eddy reserves that exalted place to herself.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commentary: part of a broader pattern of Mrs. Eddy concentrating offices and honors in her person.

rubrics_metrics.name: Science and Health as perpetual Pastor / Pastor-Universal
rubrics_metrics.description: Mrs. Eddy's book Science and Health is effectively appointed the permanent Pastor of The First Church and of all branch Churches; it is presented as the Holy Ghost, the Comforter, 'the Official Pastor and Infallible and Unerring Guide.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Author notes the book is constantly revised (many editions), yet treated as infallible; the text uses this to satirize the replacement of living pastoral authority with a printed, centrally edited text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Control of publishing profits and personnel
rubrics_metrics.description: Profits from the publishing operations go semi-annually to the Treasurer of the Mother-Church (whom the author says Mrs. Eddy 'owns'); editors and publishers cannot be elected or removed without Mrs. Eddy's knowledge/consent; employment candidates must be accepted by Mrs. Eddy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Author links these rules to consolidation of revenue and appointment power in Mrs. Eddy's hands; part of the general critique of personal ownership of institutional mechanisms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Shrine / museum usage rules and restricted visitation
rubrics_metrics.description: In the First Church there is a 'Mother's Room' or shrine containing objects (a chair, mantelpiece, painted windows, copies of books, etc.) displayed under supervision: admissions limited (four persons at a time, five minutes each), a guide ('show-woman') announces objects, chairs protected by satin ribbon, and relics are venerated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Author juxtaposes the shrine's commercialized, controlled presentation with traditional pilgrimage relics and condemns the practice as quasi-worship of the leader; gives quoted visitor account to show rules and theatricality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Frequent revision of Science and Health
rubrics_metrics.description: Science and Health has many editions (the author cites 'two hundred and fifty-eight editions') with numerous verbal changes, transpositions, and insertions; there is no index and the book is revised so often that editions differ substantially.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Author uses this to ridicule the claim of infallibility and to imply arbitrary, slipshod editorial practice; he also lampoons the self-congratulating journal language praising the 'herculean efforts' of revision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duty to circulate and sell Science and Health (command)
rubrics_metrics.description: Mrs. Eddy declared in the Christian Science Journal: 'It shall be the duty of all Christian Scientists to circulate and to sell as many of these books as they can.' The First Church added a threat that failure to obey 'will render him liable to lose his membership in this Church. MARY BAKER EDDY.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Author interprets this as effectively forcing unpaid canvassing and making book-selling a compulsory church duty under penalty of excommunication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Price and profit practices for Science and Health
rubrics_metrics.description: Science and Health price: three dollars in cloth, six dollars when finely bound; margin of profit above cost estimated at 500–700 percent. In the trade, canvassers might take 60% commission, but Mrs. Eddy's organisation uses unpaid members to canvass.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Author uses these numbers to argue that the book is a profit center exploited via members' compulsory distribution labor, pointing to high margins and organizational coercion.
